obligations.text: Establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system across the system's lifecycle.
Develop the system using training, validation and testing data sets that meet data governance and quality criteria, including bias examination and mitigation.
Draw up and keep up to date technical documentation, with at least the Annex IV elements, before placing the system on the market.
Ensure the system technically allows automatic recording of events (logs) over its lifetime.
Design the system to be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret and use its output.
Accompany the system with instructions for use containing the required information for deployers.
Design the system so natural persons can effectively oversee it, including being able to disregard or override its output and to guard against automation bias.
Achieve and declare an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout the lifecycle.
Complete the conformity assessment based on internal control (Annex VI) before placing the system on the market, and repeat it after a substantial modification.
Register yourself and the system in the EU database before placing it on the market or putting it into service.

key_facts: The tool screens and ranks job applicants' CVs
It shortlists the top candidates for recruiters
to_confirm: Confirm that recruiters review the shortlist and keep the ability to override it.
Confirm you are the provider (you developed the tool and place it on the market under your name), not just a deployer.
Confirm whether the tool profiles applicants. If it does, the Art 6(3) derogation would not be available.

obligations.text: Design and develop the chatbot so shoppers are informed they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the context.

key_facts: Customer-service chatbot on an e-commerce website
Answers shopper questions in natural language
Interacts directly with shoppers
to_confirm: Confirm the chatbot only handles customer-service queries and does not make decisions such as credit or eligibility assessments.
Confirm the chatbot does not use manipulative or subliminal techniques.
If you are the deployer and not the provider, check that the AI disclosure is built in or added.

obligations.text: Take measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy for staff who operate and use the system (not a requirement specific to minimal-risk systems).
Optionally follow voluntary codes of conduct for applying specific requirements.

key_facts: AI spam filter
Sorts incoming company email into inbox or junk
to_confirm: Confirm the filter is not also used to monitor or evaluate employees, for example by profiling their behaviour or performance.
Confirm the filter only sorts email and does not block or act on critical communications in a way that serves another purpose.

obligations.text: Establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system.
Develop the model on training, validation and testing data sets that meet the data quality criteria.
Draw up and keep up to date technical documentation before placing the system on the market or putting it into service.
Ensure the system technically allows automatic recording of events (logs) over its lifetime.
Design the system to be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret and use its output.
Accompany the system with instructions for use containing the required information for deployers.
Design the system so natural persons can effectively oversee it while it is in use.
Achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, and keep it consistent throughout the lifecycle.
Carry out the conformity assessment based on internal control (Annex VI) before placing the system on the market.

key_facts: The model scores loan applicants' creditworthiness
The bank uses the score to decide who gets a loan
to_confirm: Confirm the system scores natural persons (individual applicants), not only businesses.
Confirm the system is not used solely to detect financial fraud, which Annex III(5)(b) excludes.

obligations.text: Do not develop, place on the market, put into service or use this social scoring system.

key_facts: Government system scores each citizen's trustworthiness from everyday behaviour
The score is used to grant or deny access to public services
to_confirm: Confirm that the score's effects on access to services are not limited to a justified, proportionate response within the context where the data was collected. The description suggests they are not.

key_facts: The AI system evaluates students' exam answers
It assigns grades that decide whether students progress to the next year
to_confirm: Confirm the AI output is not limited to a purely preparatory or narrow procedural task. The description says it assigns the grades that decide progression.

key_facts: The AI assesses asylum seekers' applications
It flags a risk level for each applicant
Border officials receive and use the output
to_confirm: Confirm the system is used by or on behalf of competent public authorities (e.g. border or asylum authorities).
Confirm the use is permitted under relevant Union or national law.
Check whether the risk flag is based on prohibited practices, such as biometric categorisation or profiling that is banned.

obligations.text: As provider, ensure the app's video outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated.
As deployer, disclose that the deep fake video content has been artificially generated or manipulated.

key_facts: The app generates realistic AI videos of real public figures
The videos show them saying things they never said
The videos are used for advertising campaigns
to_confirm: Whether the app is used to deceive or manipulate people in ways that could fall under a prohibited practice in Art 5, for example by distorting behaviour and causing significant harm.
Whether the public figures have consented. The Act does not settle this, but other EU and national law such as personality rights, GDPR and advertising rules may apply.
Whether any ad use falls under the artistic, satirical or creative carve-out, which only limits how the disclosure is made.
Whether the app is used for political or electoral campaigning, which other rules may cover.

rows.clarifying_question: What is the specific intended purpose of the AI tool, meaning what task it performs, what data it processes, and who uses its output? For example, does it screen job applicants, evaluate employees, score credit, or generate content or chat with users?
key_facts: The description says only that the company is building an AI tool for internal company use

obligations.text: As provider, ensure the generated image and text outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated.
As deployer, disclose that image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake is artificially generated or manipulated.

key_facts: The system generates marketing images and ad copy from a text brief
The output is used on the company's social media
to_confirm: Whether you are the provider of the system (for example you build it or put it on the market under your name) or only a deployer using a third-party tool. This decides whether Art 50(2) or Art 50(4) applies to you.
Whether any images realistically depict real people, places or events, which would make them deep fakes that need disclosure.
Whether the system only performs an assistive editing function or does not substantially alter the input, which would exempt it from the marking duty.

key_facts: Internal research model, trained and tested in the lab only
Never placed on the market
Never used on real users
to_confirm: The model is never supplied to deployers or used outside the lab, including for your own operational use.
No testing in real-world conditions is planned. That would fall outside the exclusion and need to meet Art 57 or Art 60.
Research and development must still follow other applicable Union law, such as GDPR for training data.

obligations.text: No mandatory obligations apply, but providers and deployers should ensure staff have sufficient AI literacy.

key_facts: The system only detects duplicate job applications so a recruiter can remove them
It does not score, rank or evaluate candidates
to_confirm: The system performs no profiling of natural persons, because profiling would make it high-risk regardless of the derogation.
The system only matches duplicates and does not influence which candidates are advanced or rejected.
The provider documents its Art 6(3) assessment and registers the system, as the Act requires for Annex III systems treated as not high-risk.

rows.clarifying_question: What specific task does the AI perform in your hiring process (for example, drafting job ads, filtering or ranking applicants, scoring interviews), how is its output used, and who acts on it (for example, does a recruiter make the decision, or is the output applied automatically)?
key_facts: AI is used somewhere in the hiring process

key_facts: AI chatbot on a careers page
It screens applicants
It decides who advances to interview
to_confirm: Confirm whether you are the provider (developer or supplier) or only a deployer of a third-party tool, as the obligations differ.
Confirm that the system is not limited to a narrow procedural or preparatory task, since the description says it decides who advances.

obligations.text: Do not develop for this purpose, place on the market, put into service or use this system for predicting criminal offence risk based solely on profiling or personality traits.

key_facts: The system predicts how likely an individual is to commit a crime.
It uses only personal traits and background.
Police use it to decide who to watch.
to_confirm: Confirm that no objective and verifiable facts directly linked to a criminal activity are used as inputs. Even if they were, the system would still be high-risk under Annex III(6).

obligations.text: Take measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy among staff and others who operate or use the system on your behalf (no other mandatory obligations). You may also follow voluntary codes of conduct.

key_facts: AI grammar and spell-checker
Suggests fixes while the user types in a word processor
to_confirm: Confirm the product only suggests corrections and does not generate substantial new text, which could bring transparency duties into play.
Confirm it is not marketed for a high-risk purpose, such as grading exams or screening job applicants.

obligations.text: Do not develop, place on the market, put into service or use this system.

key_facts: Real-time facial recognition of people in public squares
Feed is streamed to the police
to_confirm: Confirm that no narrow exception applies. That would need use limited to a targeted search for victims or missing persons, a specific imminent threat, or a suspect of an Annex II offence. It would also need prior authorisation and national law permitting it, under Art 5(2).

obligations.text: Do not develop for this purpose, place on the market, put into service or use the AI system to infer employees' emotions in the workplace.

key_facts: The tool reads employees' facial expressions during meetings
It scores employees' mood, which means it infers their emotions
It is used in the workplace
to_confirm: Confirm the tool is not intended for a medical or safety purpose. Nothing in the description suggests it is, and the exception is narrow.

The credit scores decide loan approvals

obligations.text: Do not develop for this purpose, place on the market, put into service or use this biometric categorisation system.

key_facts: The tool does real-time biometric categorisation
It infers people's ethnicity and religion from their faces
to_confirm: The law-enforcement carve-out in Art 5(1)(g) covers only labelling or filtering of lawfully acquired biometric datasets. Confirm the tool does not fit that carve-out, because live inference of ethnicity and religion from faces would not.
